Yam-Akara

Overview

Yam-Akara is a magician and Brissen’s friend on Ingos. His inexpensive runes anger Karansul. Wrongly accused of murder, he helps Kir investigate his movements and uses the governor’s library during his confinement. After his release he explains how its old records reveal a hidden route to Jigran. [1, 2, 3, 4]

Two magicians on Ingos

Kir and Kel seek magical help on Ingos. Karansul complains about Yam-Akara, whose cheap runes undercut his trade, and identifies Rinas as the governor’s court magician. His receives the travellers with suspicion and later asks them to retrieve materials from his laboratory. Sver the Trapper offers another route: contact Grey Leaf through the Sacred Flower and a vessel from his cache. Grey Leaf explains that the knight Brissen and his magician friend have left for the settlement near the mines. Kir’s first task here is finding an informed ally, before the murder that later dominates the investigation. The vessel Sver asks them to carry is for Woodsfolk balm that eases his own aching joints. He has used their necessary visit to obtain a personal favour. [1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10]

The Beastmasters and the empty caravan

At the Beastmasters’ settlement, Crooked accuses Kir and Kel of being spies. Geraldine agrees to test them. Their attempt to obtain a gold nugget from a caravan finds an empty chest, making their return dangerous. Trickster reasons that genuine thieves would not come back empty-handed, and Geraldine accepts them. Advice from Trickster, also passed on by Sver if Kir consults him, about an ice elemental in the abandoned mines provides something to offer Yam-Akara. His work and the governor’s permit requirements then draw the travellers into further dealings with the court. The missing nugget will matter again when the apparent caravan failure becomes evidence of a separate theft. [11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18]

Yam-Akara’s research and the governor’s gift

Yam-Akara introduces himself as a practising magician of the first rank and an honorary member of the Assembly of Magicians of Three Worlds. The elemental samples interest him, and the Joon artifact promises material for a scholarly report. He agrees to search while Kir renews his permit for the mines, where Wormface magic interferes with his measurements. His summons the travellers to Governor Valrasian whether or not his own laboratory errand is complete. The governor demands proper introductions, pays unwelcome attention to Kel and hints at a rare Blue Clan mage’s dart for his collection. Bringing the dart wins the permit, despite his complaints about Yam-Akara’s visits. [18, 14, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23]

Brissen’s murder and the failed alibi

Green leaves around the settlement lead Kir to Grey Leaf, who brings the news. Brissen is murdered and Yam-Akara is accused of killing his old friend. Kir and Kel undertake the defence. The magician says he spent the day in the mines and arrived late for their meeting. Soldier confirms that he allowed the elderly visitor through with an expired permit and stamped it that day. Kir finds the lost pass, but Valrasian rejects the water-damaged document because the signature and date can no longer be read. This evidence supports the search but does not free Yam-Akara; the travellers still have to identify the murderer. [24, 2, 25, 26, 3, 27, 28]

Crooked’s confession

The settlement’s missing communal money supplies the decisive motive. Kir and Kel catch Crooked at his cache. Brissen had discovered the theft, so Crooked killed him. He also stole His’s knife and the gold nugget, informed on the caravan raid and later planted the knife to shift suspicion. His called the same informant to clear his own name; Crooked mistook that invitation for a trap and killed him too. Woodsfolk observations help reconstruct the planted evidence. Before the governor, Kir explains the connected crimes and Crooked admits them. Yam-Akara is released, while the governor reserves Crooked’s punishment for trial. Kel draws the thief out by spreading word that they have found the hidden money. Afterwards the travellers return the recovered communal funds to Geraldine and Trickster. Geraldine wants personal revenge, but Crooked is already in the governor’s custody. [29, 30, 31, 32, 33, 4, 34]

The hidden portal to Jigran

During his confinement, Yam-Akara gains access to the governor’s library. Old exploration reports reveal that the powerful “artifact” is a forgotten passage to another land. Trickster offers a key to the gate, then sends Kir on a fruitless ore search so that he can work without interference. With the key ready, Yam-Akara warns that he cannot sense the destination: the portal may be defective or concealed by a powerful absorbing spell. Kir recognises the same absence Tka-Rik described and concludes that it leads to Jigran. He decides to go directly, trusting the strength gained during his journey. Kel chooses to accompany him again. [4, 35, 36, 37]
